title: The Rebel's Silhouette: Selected Poems (ghazals and lyrics)

tone_mechanisms_observed: ghazal form: autonomous couplets held together by refrain (radif) and rhyme (qafiya)
grief and longing sustained as an unresolved present
ambiguity between erotic, political, and mystical registers of sorrow
repetition of the refrain as a returning ache rather than narrative progress
public grief (war, exile) folded into personal grief
mechanics.emotional_progression: Non-linear: each couplet is thematically complete, producing accumulation rather than an arc, which is itself an elegiac effect.
mechanics.point_of_view: Lyric 'I' that is both personal and representative.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Urdu quantitative metre and refrain; the English free-verse translations preserve meaning but not sound, a stated translation limit.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Conventional ghazal imagery allows intimate grief to be spoken under a social mask.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Modern Urdu ghazal's grief register; cross-linked as an Indian/regional tradition. Verified via UMass Press and Poetry Foundation commentary. Described, not quoted.
mechanics.copyright_note: Poems and translations copyrighted. Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
